:::note[About this page]
This page is generated from the `tools/list` response of [s1000d-reader-mcp](/s1000d-stack/mcp/reader-mcp/) 0.13.0. The s1000d-reader-mcp page explains the configuration and how to read the responses.
:::

## Summary

Reads one data module as structure: the identification and status section, the content tree, references (with titles) and the verification status. When `product` is passed, each block is marked `applicable` / `notApplicable` / `undetermined`. With `includeLocation: true`, every node carries `location` (`path`, `line`, `column`)

## Description returned by `tools/list`

This is the text an LLM receives.

> Read one data module as structure, not XML: identification and status (DMC, issue, language, title, BREX ref, QA, DM-level applicability), the body as a tree of blocks (sections, paragraphs, lists, tables, figures with ICN, warnings/cautions/notes, numbered steps, requirements; processes and fault isolation too), the references it makes, ALWAYS a "verification" status (XSD by default) and ALWAYS "securityClassification" (the data module's value and the values carried by elements in the body, uninterpreted) at the top of the response. section "outline" returns a summary (headings, step numbers, first sentence, size of each subtree) for deciding what to read. Applicability of each block is evaluated for the given product (applicable / notApplicable / undetermined); without a product, only display texts are returned — assert expressions are never returned.

## Arguments

The content of `inputSchema`. A nested argument is written as `parent.child`, and an item of an array as `parent[].child`.

| Name | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` |  |  | File path of the document. |
| `xml` | `string` |  |  | The document as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB). |
| `dmc` | `string` |  |  | DMC of the data module to read from the CSDB (e.g. "S1000DBIKE-AAA-D00-00-00-00AA-041A-A"; "DMC-" prefix optional). Alternative to path/xml. |
| `csdbDirs` | `array<string>` |  |  | CSDB folders to search for data modules by DMC, referenced objects, ACT/CCT/PCT and BREX (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes. |
| `product` | `object` |  |  | The product to evaluate applicability for. attributes: ACT productAttribute id → value (e.g. {"model": "Brook trekker", "version": "Mk9"}); conditions: CCT cond id → value. Omit to get "undetermined" with display texts only. Use describe_applicability to learn the available ids and values. |
| `product.attributes` | `object` |  |  |  |
| `product.conditions` | `object` |  |  |  |
| `section` | `string` |  | `identAndStatus` / `content` / `all` / `outline`, default `"all"` | Which part to return (default all). "outline" returns only headings, step numbers, the first sentence and the size (nodes / chars / admonitions) of each subtree — call it first on a large data module to decide what to read. |
| `includeLocation` | `boolean` |  |  | Add "location" (path, line, column) to every node of the body or the outline (default false). Pass true when you are going to edit the data module with s1000d-writer-mcp edit_data_module: its "at" and "to" take location.path as returned here. A step also gets "textLocations": the locations of the paragraphs joined into its "text", in order. |
| `outlineDepth` | `integer` |  |  | With section "outline": how many levels of headings / steps to return (default: all levels). |
| `verify` | `string` |  | `schema` / `full` / `none`, default `"schema"` | How much to verify before reading: "schema" (default) runs XSD validation only; "full" also checks BREX along the brexDmRef chain and resolves references; "none" skips verification (reported as not-run). |
| `omitNotApplicable` | `boolean` |  | default `false` | Drop blocks that are notApplicable for the given product (default false: keep them, marked). The number dropped is reported. |
| `maxNodes` | `number` |  | default `5000` | Cap on body nodes returned (default 5000). |
